title: Sinai (Exodus 19)
hookLine: thunder, smoke, a trumpet, and a people told you shall be my own

cards: Three months out of Egypt, they come to a mountain in the desert and camp at its foot. It's the mountain of the burning bush, where Moses was told he'd bring the people to worship.
Now here they all are, a nation of former slaves, tents across the plain, looking up. And on the third morning, the mountain disappears into a cloud. Thunder.
Lightning. A trumpet blast that keeps getting louder. Smoke rising off the top like a furnace.
The ground shaking. Everyone in the camp trembles.

teach.h: I CARRIED YOU ON EAGLES' WINGS.
teach.b: Before the thunder comes a message. God tells Moses to say to the people: you've seen what I did to Egypt, and how I carried you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself.
Deuteronomy later fills in that picture: an eagle stirring up her nest, spreading her wings, catching her young and carrying them. Not a cage. A carrying.
Second, the promise. If you keep my covenant, God says, you'll be my own treasured possession among all the peoples, for all the earth is mine.
The Hebrew word is segullah, a king's word for his private treasure. And then: you'll be a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. The people answer together: all that the Lord has spoken, we will do.
Three days to get ready. Wash your clothes. Don't touch the mountain.
Then the cloud comes down, and the people stand back trembling while Moses goes up into it. Fourth, how Catholics hear it.

teach.h: A KINGLY PRIESTHOOD, A HOLY NATION.
teach.b: Peter's first letter gives these very words to the baptized: "But you are a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood, a holy nation, a purchased people."
The Church calls this the common priesthood of all the faithful: every baptized person belongs to a people that is God's, and offers the world back to God. And another echo.
Jewish tradition came to link the feast of Shavuot, fifty days after Passover, with the giving of the law at Sinai.
On that same feast, Pentecost, the Spirit came down on the apostles with wind, fire and a sound from heaven.

how: The Catholic Church teaches that every baptized person shares in the common priesthood of the faithful, drawing on Exodus 19:6 and 1 Peter 2:9, and at Pentecost the Church remembers the Spirit coming with wind and fire.

s: at Sinai, the people climb the mountain with Moses
they're told not even to touch it. they stand trembling at the foot while Moses goes up into the cloud.
Sinai is the same mountain where Moses saw the burning bush
he was told he'd bring the people back to worship there.

the letter takes the words of Exodus 19 and gives them to the Church.

games.q: you're one of the people at the foot of Sinai. Moses comes down with God's offer: you'll be my own treasure, a kingdom of priests. how do the people answer?
o: all that the Lord has spoken, we will do.
games.why: they answer together: all that the Lord has spoken, we will do. then come three days of getting ready.

practice: See a mountain, rough and enormous, its top wrapped in a cloud you can't see into; hear the wind, and feel the ground under you, solid, then slightly trembling.

You're at the foot with thousands of others, not at the top, and that's fine: the people stood at the foot too. If you pray, stay there in silence before God; if you don't, simply stay with the picture and notice the awe.

wordCard.voice: Sinai. The mountain of the burning bush, wrapped in cloud and thunder, where God named a rescued people his own. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: treasured possession, a king's private treasure. God's word for Israel in Exodus 19:5.

carryVoice: Your line: a people of his own. Carried on eagles' wings, and called treasure. Day three hundred seventy-seven.
